decision: Choose review-all or calibrated triage for the same eligible contract workload.
primary_outcome: Total inference, review, QA and rework cost per eligible contract, with accepted-error risk reported independently.
denominator: All eligible assigned contracts, including failures and retries; report clause-level errors separately from contract cost.
independence_unit: Contract for retrospective validation; reviewer team for a workflow trial if teammates share routing or training.
quality_guardrail: Accepted-error risk bound, review capacity and material-error rate. Do not infer incident dollar severity from clause labels.
minimum_data: Contract and clause IDs, assignment, model/policy version, review minutes, inference charges, QA/rework events, truth provenance and material-error adjudication.
failure_handling: Keep failed contracts and retry costs. Unadjudicated outputs remain unknown; compare conservative error bounds before auto-acceptance.
release_rule: Require quality gates and lower review-adjusted cost under measured workload; the assumed economic model alone does not approve automation.
reversal: Exception time, residual error or integration cost eliminates the advantage, or no threshold meets the risk ceiling.
status: PROPOSED MEASUREMENT CONTRACT; NOT AN EXECUTED DOMAIN EXPERIMENT
defense: No. It is a retrospective model-validation result. Financial return additionally needs measured review effort, deployment cost and error exposure.
Clauses from one contract share context. Splitting those clauses across training and validation can leak information and overstate generalization.
